attackPath: Handler exception to HTTP 500 JSON; generic handler also emitted exception name/code to console.
rootCause: Raw exception messages were treated as safe response text; arbitrary name/code fields were treated as safe diagnostics.
impact: Credential-like data or PII in an exception could cross the response/log boundary. Actual historical attacker access remains UNKNOWN.
repair: Fixed response and diagnostic strings; existing database 503/504 branch retained.
negativeTest: Synthetic exceptions carry a marker in message, name and code; neither response nor captured logs may contain it.

evidence.layer: Controlled direct handler, explicit in-memory storage

remainingLimitations: Not all dependency classification or 503/504 serialization tested here
No real provider/deployed log/browser telemetry proof
Error diagnostics need correlation at server request layer
Other admin authorization, storage, export and PII boundaries remain incomplete
